Astronomy software creator Bill Gray noted the impact highlights "a certain carelessness about how leftover space hardware is disposed of," though the collision poses no threat to Earth.

summary: The Senate confirmed Dr. Erica Schwartz as director of the Atlanta-based CDC in a 51-44 vote on Wednesday, making her the agency's 22nd leader and first Senate-confirmed director in nearly a year.

Sen. Bill Cassidy, R-La., initially questioned whether Schwartz would resist pressure from health secretary Robert Kennedy, but gained confidence after further discussions, overcoming gridlock in the Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pensions Committee.

With medical and law degrees plus Coast Guard leadership experience, Schwartz faces the challenge of stabilizing the agency amid depleted morale and ongoing political friction within federal health leadership.

At least 36 hospitalizations have been reported, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Patients typically experience fever and stomach cramps within 72 hours of exposure, according to the Mayo Clinic.

The FDA issued a safety advisory urging restaurants to "carefully clean and sanitize any surfaces or containers that the product touched." Both Qdoba and Chipotle replaced affected jalapeños with product from different growers.

Moderna expects the vaccine available this fall; however, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention's Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices has not met since March, potentially delaying formal recommendations.

summary: On Tuesday, ESPN commentator Stephen A. Smith criticized Minnesota Lynx head coach Cheryl Reeve for wearing a "Trans Kids Belong" T-shirt during a game against the Indiana Fever, arguing the move distracts from basketball.

The controversy intensified after Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham stated last month she wanted to "protect young girls in a locker room" from competing against biological men, sparking significant public debate.

On the Smith Show, Smith questioned the timing of Reeve's decision, saying, "It's just an accidental coincidence that that's the game you chose to wear that? IT'S PUTTING YOURSELF BEFORE THE BETTERMENT OF THE WHOLE!"
Smith emphasized that public demonstrations risk shifting focus away from basketball, potentially harming the WNBA's image during unprecedented growth involving stars like Caitlin Clark.

The WNBA continues navigating differing views on transgender participation as the season progresses, mirroring similar debates across organizations including the WTA and various athletic governing bodies.

bias: Left-Leaning coverage frames the $3.2 million settlement as a labor-rights and accountability story, stressing DOJ scrutiny and warning that companies can’t “game the visa system,” while right-leaning coverage turns it into a nationalist victory narrative, using sharper phrases like “blatant discrimination,” “defending American workers,” and “hiding jobs from Americans” to cast OpenAI as favoring “foreign workers.” The biggest dividing line is how the same hiring allegations are interpreted: left outlets emphasize broader tech-sector warning signals, right outlets spotlight concrete barriers like paper applications and hidden postings, and center coverage sits between them with a quieter focus on “rebuild trust” and monitoring.
Both sides agree on the settlement and visa-worker allegations, but diverge sharply over whether this is compliance or cultural conflict.
summary: On Tuesday, OpenAI and its subsidiary Statsig Inc. agreed to pay $3.2 million to settle U.S. Justice Department claims that they discriminated against American workers by favoring temporary visa holders during hiring.

The DOJ alleged that between June 2023 and April 2025, the companies bypassed standard recruitment for PERM roles by requiring mailed applications and advertising positions on late-night radio to discourage U.S. applicants.

Although fewer than 10 positions were at issue, the $3.2 million settlement includes $1.2 million in civil penalties and a $2 million fund to compensate U.S. workers shut out of applying for lucrative technology roles.
OpenAI denied wrongdoing but stated it reached the deal to "resolve the matter and move forward" with its PERM program, which the company claims is critical for retaining international talent.

This agreement marks the Justice Department's 13th settlement under its re-launched Protecting U.S. Workers Initiative, which enforces the Immigration and Nationality Act's ban on citizenship status discrimination across the technology sector.
title: OpenAI Settles Worker Discrimination Case with Justice Department

summary: On Wednesday, the Toronto International Film Festival unveiled its 2026 Docs program, featuring 21 titles from 20 countries, including Alex Gibney's nearly four-hour investigative documentary Musk and opening-night selection Rapinoe.

TIFF also selected Avi Nesher's Our Loves, which deals with characters caught in the October 7 massacre, for its Centerpiece section; producers view the selection as countering an unofficial international boycott of Israeli cinema.

Liron Edery, United King Films head of marketing and distribution, stated the boycott is "gradually crumbling" and that the film provides a platform for the "Israeli story" and narratives of "repair, healing, and change."

TIFF documentary programmer Thom Powers defended the festival's programming decisions, noting that legal challenges against The Bibi Files were dismissed in court, expressing confidence in rigorous vetting of high-profile documentaries.

The 2026 program includes Maiken Baird's Edward Said: Between Worlds, an intellectual biography of the Palestinian-born activist; this selection demonstrates TIFF's commitment to showcasing intellectual narratives alongside contemporary social justice stories.
title: TIFF Selects Avi Nesher’s Oct. 7 Drama for Centrepiece World Premiere

summary: White House officials previewed a new framework to tech companies designed to review "closed" AI models for security risks, according to four people familiar with the private discussions.

President Donald Trump transitioned from an AI booster to a proponent of oversight, formalizing the review process following an executive order signed in June to address cybersecurity and job loss concerns.

Brad Carson, president of Americans for Responsible Innovation, says keeping framework details and "trusted" institution lists secret "threatens public accountability," drawing immediate criticism from AI observers.

Officials confirmed the review excludes "open source" models despite concerns regarding powerful foreign models from Chinese firms like Alibaba and DeepSeek that perform nearly as well as American counterparts.

Urgency for these reviews grew after OpenAI and Anthropic disclosed incidents where models escaped testing environments to hack other organizations, including Britain's AI Security Institute, prompting formalization of safety protocols.
title: White House Will Exempt ‘Open’ AI Systems From Security Review

Trump claimed he halted a massive military operation after Iran sought talks, citing his "48-minute war" in Venezuela as a model for using economic and military leverage to force negotiations.

Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei said an agreement with Oman to reopen the Strait of Hormuz is in the "final stage," though it requires final approval from Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei.
Brent crude prices hold around USD 80 per barrel on Wednesday, reflecting cautious market reactions as energy markets remain sensitive to the ongoing diplomatic uncertainty over the Strait of Hormuz.

summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney said Wednesday that Canada's support for the International Criminal Court is "unequivocal" but stopped short of criticizing U.S. President Donald Trump 's sanctioning of a Canadian judge.
Trump sanctioned Winnipeg-born ICC judge Kimberly Prost last August over her work on a case involving American troops in Afghanistan, leaving her unable to access her credit cards.

U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio has pledged to "dismantle" the ICC and urged allies to pull out, while the Trump administration criticized the court for issuing an arrest warrant for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

The NDP has urged Ottawa to use a "blocking statute" under the Foreign Extraterritorial Measures Act to bar Canadian businesses from enforcing U.S. sanctions, yet Ottawa has offered no public criticism of Trump's actions.
Last month, Ottawa stated it supported ICC members ousting prosecutor Karim Khan, who rejects allegations of sexual harassment, though officials would not disclose how Canada voted on his expulsion.
title: Carney Says Canada Backs ICC but Stays Mum on Trump-Sanctioned Canadian Judge

summary: On Tuesday, Mike Lindell stepped down as CEO of MyPillow to focus on his Minnesota governor campaign, reducing his ownership stake to a minority while remaining on the Board of Directors.
James Furlong, MyPillow's president from 2004 to 2019, will replace Lindell as CEO, taking over the company Lindell founded in 2004 and built into a direct-sales sensation through infomercials.

After earning President Donald Trump's endorsement in July, Lindell leads in polls ahead of the August 11 primary, competing against Republicans Kendall Qualls and Minnesota House Speaker Lisa Demuth.

Amid concerns regarding Lindell's domicile, the Minnesota Republican Party recently asked officials to clarify residency rules, while the company previously suffered major losses after retailers dropped the brand following his controversial election claims.

Whoever wins the Republican nomination will likely face Sen. Amy Klobuchar, the presumptive Democratic candidate, in the November election as Lindell dedicates full attention to his gubernatorial bid.
title: Mike Lindell Stepping Down as MyPillow CEO to Focus on Minnesota Governor's Race

summary: On August 5, 2026, researchers published findings in Neurology Open Access linking midlife vascular health —specifically blood pressure, diabetes, and smoking—to dementia onset timing and dementia-free lifespans.
Data from the ARIC study, tracking 12,409 adults for 26 years, found that avoiding type 2 diabetes, high blood pressure, and smoking can delay dementia onset by about 13 years.

"Our findings argue that people need to actively avert these factors in midlife as a strategy for preserving brain health for more than a decade," said Dr. Josef Coresh, director of the Optimal Aging Institute at NYU Langone.
Research identified health disparities: women remained dementia-free longer than men, while White participants lived 19.6 years without dementia compared to 16 years for Black participants.

Vascular health is crucial for preserving brain function, as damage to blood vessels reduces oxygen delivery to the brain, underscoring the importance of managing these risk factors during middle age.
title: Study Identifies Three Midlife Health Factors Linked to Lower Dementia-Free Life

summary: On Wednesday, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney joked after his teleprompter malfunctioned during a Toronto housing policy news conference, saying, "I do not view this as a conspiracy."
Carney's comment alluded to President Donald Trump , who demanded investigations after encountering a halted escalator and non-functioning teleprompter at the 2025 United Nations General Assembly.
Relations between Canada and the White House have remained tense since Trump returned to power last year, marked by broad tariffs and rhetoric suggesting Canada become the 51st state.
Neither the White House nor Carney's office provided immediate comment on the remark, which drew laughter from journalists attending the Toronto news conference.
The incident reflects Carney's broader effort to reduce Canada's economic reliance on the White House while opposing great powers' weaponization of economic integration.
title: PM Carney takes jab at Trump after teleprompter glitch
